AMZN.rationale: Amazon's franchise is elite and improving: AWS reaccelerated to 28% YoY growth in Q1 2026 (fastest in 15 quarters), operating margin hit a record 13.1%, and the custom chip business reached a $20B run rate. The balance sheet is a fortress (0.149 D/E, $369.63B equity). However, the stock has already re-rated to near-peak PE multiples (37.6x vs 28.2-40.9x 365-day range) after a 25-30% rally in 30 days, and the quant report's Q3 2025 operating margin compression (9.7%) — though reversed in Q1 2026 — signals that the prior quarter's earnings quality was deteriorating. FCF has collapsed to $1.2B TTM due to $220B capex guidance, creating a multi-year 'prove it' cycle. The 2.7% earnings yield vs 4.40% 10-year rate demands near-perfect execution. Oil at $108.64/bbl adds logistics cost risk. The Q1 2026 Anthropic investment gains ($16.8B pre-tax) inflate EPS similarly to Q3 2025's non-operating items, raising recurring-earnings questions. Net: strong franchise with positive trajectory, but valuation is stretched vs own history and the recent rally has priced in much of the good news, leaving limited upside at current levels absent further fundamental beats.
key_factors: AWS reacceleration to 28% YoY growth in Q1 2026, fastest in 15 quarters, $150B annualized run rate
Record 13.1% operating margin in Q1 2026, reversing Q3 2025's 9.7% compression
PE at 37.6x near top of 28.2-40.9x 365-day range after 25-30% rally in 30 days
FCF collapsed to $1.2B TTM due to $220B capex guidance (up from $200B), creating prove-it cycle
Custom chip business (Trainium/Inferentia) at $20B annual run rate growing triple digits
Anthropic $5B investment with $100B+ decade-long spending commitment; $16.8B pre-tax gains inflate Q1 EPS
Earnings yield 2.7% vs 10-year Treasury 4.40% — 170bp negative spread demands high growth
Oil at $108.64/bbl (+76% over 90 days) creates logistics cost headwind
Balance sheet fortress: 0.149 D/E, $369.63B equity, $55.10B debt
California antitrust price-fixing lawsuit (April 20, 2026) and ongoing FTC case create regulatory tail risk
Advertising segment surpassing $70B TTM revenue, growing 22-24% YoY as second high-margin pillar

net_income=21.19B vs operating_income=17.42B implies ~3.77B non-operating gains inflating EPS

Net sales increased 17% to $181.5 billion in the first quarter... AWS segment sales increased 28% year-over-year to $37.6 billion... Operating income increased to $23.9 billion... Operating margin: 13.1%, highest ever.

Free cash flow decreased to $1.2 billion for the trailing twelve months, driven primarily by a year-over-year increase of $59.3 billion in purchases of property and equipment, net of proceeds from sales and incentives.
Amazon said property and equipment expenses in the first quarter reached $44.2 billion... the company announced this year's Prime Day discount bonanza will be held in June.

Amazon announced a new $5 billion investment in Anthropic... Anthropic will use Amazon's Trainium AI chips for up to 5 gigawatts of computing capacity and commit to spending over $100 billion with Amazon over the next decade.
California authorities allege Amazon employees have repeatedly worked with vendors using its platform to push retail vendors including Walmart and Chewy to set higher prices collectively.
Amazon committed approximately $200 billion in capital expenditure for full-year 2026, a 53% increase from the $131.8 billion deployed in 2025.
Amazon held an estimated 37.6% share of total U.S. e-commerce retail sales in 2025, representing more than four times the share of its closest domestic competitor

Amazon Web Services (AWS) maintained approximately 31% of the total public cloud IaaS and PaaS market by revenue in 2025, ahead of Microsoft Azure at approximately 24% and Google Cloud at approximately 12%.
